As a mom of two, babyproofing has honestly been less about making my house look “perfect” and more about creating spaces where my kids can safely explore, climb, play, and just be kids without me feeling on edge 24/7 😅

These are the babyproofing products we actually use daily and the ones that made the biggest difference for us — especially during the curious toddler stage when they somehow find danger in EVERYTHING 🫠

I tried to focus on products that are:
• practical + easy to use
• don’t completely ruin the look of your home
• actually hold up over time
• make life easier instead of more stressful

Because the reality is… you can’t watch them every second. Having a few solid systems in place gives so much peace of mind 🤍

items.caption:
We’ve made it clear that children are only welcome in public if they’re quiet.

A lot of parents aren’t handing over screens because they don’t care…they’re often trying to avoid the judgment that comes when a child cries, laughs too loudly, gets restless, or simply acts their age in public.

We’ve created a culture where children are expected to be seen, not heard. 

Then we criticize parents for using the very tools that help them meet those impossible expectations.

Maybe the solution isn’t more shame. 

Maybe it’s more patience, more understanding, and more room for kids to be kids. ❤️

I promise you, I love my son with a fiery passion. But here are some honest thoughts I had while pregnant with him. 

🖤 there is no possible way I can love another child as much as I love Adalynn. 

🖤 Did I make a terrible mistake? 

🖤 Adalynn is perfect, what will we do if this one sucks? 

🖤 I don’t know how I’ll be able to give both the love they need. 

🖤 my daughters life is going to change forever and how horrible for her. (Spoiler, she gained a bestie and is living her best life) 

I’m sharing this because I honestly couldn’t believe some of the thoughts that popped into my head- but it’s more normal than you think. And you will indeed love your second just as much as your first ❤️

What are some crazy thought you had during pregnancy? Share them in the comments!

If you learn nothing else from my account, I hope it’s that you CAN advocate for what you want when giving birth! 

Obviously, there are times when serious interventions need to happen but even then it’s OK to question why you’re being told what to do and if there’s another option. 

I was having a completely normal labor, and the triage nurses really wanted me to lay down so they could check to see how far I was dilated- little did they know I was in the middle of transition and I refused. 

They made it work and was able to quickly check and see that I was indeed 9cm dilated and needed to be rush upstairs to have the baby! 👶

#positivebirth #birthadvocate #unmedicatedbirth #birthstory #positivebirthexperience

items.caption:
You need to see this if you’re postpartum. 🤍

This is my body 2 hours after giving birth vs. 1 month postpartum.

Social media can make it seem like our bodies should “bounce back” overnight, but that’s not how healing works.

Your body spent 9 months growing a baby. It won’t heal in a few days—or even a few weeks. And that’s okay.

So if you’re feeling discouraged when you look in the mirror, this is your reminder: you are not behind. 

Your body is healing exactly the way it’s meant to.

Give yourself patience. Give yourself grace. 

Your body just did something extraordinary, and it deserves love through every stage of recovery. 🤍

#postpartum #motherhood #momsofinstagram #momssupportingmoms #postpartumbody

items.caption:
I thought the hardest part of having a second baby was going to be loving them as much as I love my first.

It wasn’t.

That was the easiest part.

The hardest part was healing from birth while my toddler still wanted me to chase her around the yard.

It was being nap-trapped with a newborn while she asked me to come build towers, push her on the swing, or watch her do “just one more thing.”

It was hearing, “Mommy, I need help!” and not being able to jump up the second she called because someone else needed me first.

It was realizing our days would never look the way they used to.

I missed her while she was sitting right next to me.

I missed the version of us that only existed before she became a big sister.

If you’re in the middle of that transition, I hope you know it’s okay to grieve what was while still being deeply grateful for what is. 

Those two feelings can live side by side.

#parenting #motherhood #momssupportingmoms #newmomlife #newmoms
